description:
FILED AND FIXED s473h (Opus, 2026-09-08), pre-existing at a9f2a264, found
while adding the guard rows Fable's review of #1249(4) asked for.

PROBE (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL at a9f2a264):

    my @c = eval (1,2,3);  print "[@c]\n";
    perl   [3]                     (the parens are eval's argument, and inside
                                    them `1,2,3` is the COMMA OPERATOR, whose
                                    value is 3)
    PCL    dies, "The value 2 is not of type LIST", inside %P-EVAL-1

  The emission was `(p-eval 1 2 3)`: the parenthesised list was split into
  THREE arguments, so `p-eval`'s `lex-alist` parameter received 2 and its
  `features` parameter 3.

  The other two spellings were already right and stay so:
    eval 1,2,3     perl 1, PCL 1   (a list operator's first element; the
                                    extra terms never became this funcall's
                                    children)
    eval((1,2,3))  perl 3, PCL 3   (the inner parens are an expression, and
                                    the emission is `(p-eval (progn 1 2 3) â¦)`)

THE FIX: `Pl::PExpr::collapse_extra_unary_params`, called from the same four
sites as its mirror `add_implicit_default_param` â too FEW parameters get the
`$_` default there, too MANY are the comma operator here.  A funcall whose
whole `known_no_of_params` spec is the named-unary one (only 0 / 1 / -2, and
at least one 1) and which has more than one parameter has them re-parented
under a `progn` node â THE SAME node type the doubly-parenthesised spelling
already produces, so there is one comma-group lowering rather than two
(rule 11).

WHY IT IS SAFE TO APPLY TO THE WHOLE NAMED-UNARY FAMILY: perl REFUSES this
shape for most of its members (`length("a","b")` is "Too many arguments for
length", `defined(1,2,3)` and `uc("a","b")` likewise â probed).  That is
INVALID perl, which PCL is not required to reject (CLAUDE.md rule 9), and
answering perl's comma-operator value there is strictly better than the SBCL
arity crash it replaces ("invalid number of arguments: 3").  List operators
(-1), `@_`-defaulting builtins (-3) and the "one before a list" spec (-12)
are excluded by the spec test, so nothing that legitimately has many children
is touched.

GUARD: `Pl/t/eval-01.t` row "eval (1,2,3) is the comma operator: eval(\"3\")",
inverse-verified â it fails on the a9f2a264 extraction.

MEASURED: corpus-diff over the 111-file perl-tests population and
emission-ab over lib/**/*.pm + cpan-tests/**/*.t + the SHAPES corpus (336
files) show the DIFF set UNCHANGED from before this commit â no file in any
population contains the shape.

=== DONE (s473h) ===
subject: FIXED s473h (pre-existing CRASH): a named-unary builtin given a PARENTHESISED LIST got N arguments instead of one comma EXPRESSION -- `eval (1,2,3)` is 3 in perl and died in PCL with an SBCL type error (p-eval's lex-alist parameter received the number 2)
